parameters.content:
## 1. Lead intake (webhook)
An authenticated endpoint other tools can post a researched lead to (for example a scheduled research agent). Invalid or duplicate leads are rejected with a clear reply; new ones land in the sheet as "New".

nodes.name: Webhook: lead intake
nodes.notes: Protected with a Header Auth credential: callers must send the secret in a header. Requests without it are rejected before any node runs.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { success: false, duplicate: $json.isDuplicate, invalid: $json.invalid, message: $json.invalid ? "Missing field: company. Nothing was saved." : "That lead already exists (same domain or company). Nothing was saved." } }}

parameters.content:
## 2. Lead discovery (weekdays 07:00)
Pulls candidates from three sources (job ads, company search, news), merges them by domain, drops blocked and already-known companies, pre-scores them with a rule-based ICP matrix, then asks the local LLM for a final score. Only leads above the minimum score reach the sheet.

parameters.jsCode:
// CONFIG for the discovery lane. This is the only place that decides who we target, what we say and how we send.
// To switch to another profile, paste the matching section from config/<profile>.json over this object.
const CONFIG = {
  "timezone": "America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires",
  "language": "en",
  "sender": {
    "name": "Your Name",
    "title": "Business Development",
    "company": "Your Company",
    "signature": "Your Name\nBusiness Development\nYour Company",
    "email": "you@example.com",
    "review_email": "you@example.com"
  },
  "models": {
    "email": "qwen2.5:14b",
    "linkedin": "qwen3:4b",
    "score": "qwen2.5:14b",
    "classify": "llama3.2:3b",
    "followup": "qwen3:4b"
  },
  "sources": {
    "adzuna": {
      "enabled": true,
      "country": "us",
      "max_days_old": 40,
      "keep_regex": "(head of sales|\\bvp\\b.{0,30}sales|vice president.{0,30}sales|director of sales|sales director|sales manager|account executive|sales development|\\bsdr\\b|\\bbdr\\b|business development (manager|executive|representative|director)|chief revenue|revenue officer|founding[^a-z]{0,25}sales)",
      "queries": [
        {
          "what": "VP of Sales",
          "where": "Texas"
        },
        {
          "what": "Head of Sales",
          "where": "Austin"
        },
        {
          "what": "Account Executive SaaS",
          "where": "Austin"
        },
        {
          "what": "Sales Manager IT services",
          "where": "Colorado"
        },
        {
          "what": "Director of Sales",
          "where": "Arizona"
        }
      ]
    },
    "apollo": {
      "enabled": true,
      "rotate_pages": 4,
      "locations": [
        "Texas, United States",
        "Colorado, United States",
        "Arizona, United States"
      ],
      "sales_titles": [
        "account executive",
        "sales manager",
        "head of sales",
        "vp of sales",
        "director of sales",
        "business development",
        "sales development representative"
      ],
      "queries": [
        {
          "vertical": "SaaS",
          "label": "saas_hiring",
          "signals": [
            "hiring_sales_role"
          ],
          "keywords": [
            "saas",
            "b2b software"
          ],
          "employee_ranges": [
            "1,10",
            "11,50"
          ],
          "job_titles": "sales_titles",
          "job_posted_days": 60
        },
        {
          "vertical": "SaaS",
          "label": "saas_funded",
          "signals": [
            "recent_funding"
          ],
          "keywords": [
            "saas",
            "b2b software"
          ],
          "employee_ranges": [
            "1,10",
            "11,50"
          ],
          "funding_days": 365
        },
        {
          "vertical": "IT services",
          "label": "it_hiring",
          "signals": [
            "hiring_sales_role"
          ],
          "keywords": [
            "managed services",
            "managed service provider",
            "it services"
          ],
          "employee_ranges": [
            "1,10",
            "11,50"
          ],
          "job_titles": "sales_titles",
          "job_posted_days": 60
        },
        {
          "vertical": "Professional services",
          "label": "profserv_hiring",
          "signals": [
            "hiring_sales_role"
          ],
          "keywords": [
            "management consulting",
            "consulting",
            "accounting",
            "legal services",
            "wealth management"
          ],
          "employee_ranges": [
            "1,10",
            "11,50"
          ],
          "job_titles": [
            "business development",
            "sales",
            "account executive",
            "client development"
          ],
          "job_posted_days": 90
        }
      ]
    },
    "news": {
      "enabled": true,
      "location_label": "US (news)",
      "based_prefixes": [
        "texas",
        "austin",
        "colorado",
        "arizona"
      ],
      "queries": [
        "Austin startup raises seed OR \"Series A\" software when:30d",
        "Texas OR Colorado \"managed service provider\" OR consulting OR \"professional services\" raises OR acquires OR expands when:30d"
      ]
    }
  },
  "blocklists": {
    "whole_word": [
      "sandler",
      "gong",
      "clari",
      "chorus",
      "outreach",
      "salesloft"
    ],
    "substring": [
      "winning by design",
      "force management",
      "sales enablement",
      "sales training",
      "sales coaching",
      "fractional cro",
      "fractional cso",
      "revops consulting",
      "recruit",
      "staffing",
      "talent acquisition",
      "headhunt",
      "executive search",
      "michael page",
      "robert half",
      "korn ferry"
    ],
    "big_corp": [
      "salesforce",
      "microsoft",
      "oracle",
      "google",
      "amazon",
      "meta",
      "workday",
      "servicenow",
      "adobe",
      "sap",
      "ibm",
      "staples",
      "uber",
      "honeywell",
      "medtronic",
      "merck",
      "labcorp",
      "pwc",
      "metlife",
      "equifax",
      "marriott",
      "deloitte",
      "accenture",
      "kpmg",
      "cvs",
      "cognizant",
      "stripe",
      "aetna",
      "wipro",
      "infosys",
      "tcs",
      "capgemini",
      "ey",
      "pepsico",
      "nestle",
      "kroger",
      "walgreens"
    ]
  },
  "icp": {
    "prompt": "You evaluate B2B leads for a services consultancy that helps founder-led companies build a repeatable sales process (ICP, playbooks, pricing, CRM, pipeline). Decide whether this company is a good prospect and return an integer score from 1 to 12.\n\nICP: United States; 1-30 employees (up to 50 with a strong signal); revenue between 500K and 5M or clear potential; founder-led, with no COO, RevOps or Sales Ops in place; verticals: B2B services and consulting, SaaS, IT services and MSPs, professional services (legal, accounting, wealth management).\n\n\"WHY NOW\" SIGNALS (positive, strongest first): 1) a posted VP/Head of Sales or first AE/SDR vacancy (strongest); 2) a first sales leader hired less than 6 months ago; 3) a recent seed or Series A round; 4) an OPEN Sales Ops/RevOps vacancy in a company under 50 people (ambiguous); 5) a fragmented stack (spreadsheets plus a CRM); 6) physical or market expansion; 7) a founder complaining about follow-ups or CRM; 8) funding in the last 12 months; 9) a sales vacancy open for more than 30 days or repeated sales hiring (the founder already tried and it did not stick); 10) news about expansion, a new location or an acquisition.\n\nHARD RULES (score 1-4): the company ALREADY has someone in a RevOps/Sales Ops/Director of Operations seat (a person in the role, not an open vacancy); a mature integrated sales stack; more than 200 employees or a nationally known corporation (score 1-2 ALWAYS, whatever the role; when unsure whether a company is large and well known, assume it is and lower the score); a direct competitor (growth or RevOps consultancy, fractional CRO/CSO, sales enablement or training); procurement or buying-committee processes.\n\nCONSISTENCY: the score cannot be 8 or higher unless \"why\" cites a concrete signal from the list, not a generic phrase.\nDO NOT INVENT: use only the information provided.\nIf there is no sales vacancy (empty role) but the firmographics fit, it is a weaker lead: maximum score 6 unless the description shows another concrete signal.",
    "signal_weights": {
      "hiring_sales_role": 3,
      "hiring_sales_manager": 3,
      "recent_funding": 3,
      "founder_closing": 3,
      "stale_vacancy": 2,
      "repeat_sales_hiring": 2,
      "expansion": 2,
      "referral_dependent": 2,
      "no_sales_function": 2,
      "new_sales_leader": 1,
      "acquisition": 1,
      "crm_spreadsheets": 1
    },
    "home_region_regex": "texas|austin|,\\s*tx\\b",
    "revenue_ideal": [
      500000,
      5000000
    ],
    "employees_ok": [
      3,
      30
    ],
    "founder_led_max_employees": 15
  },
  "limits": {
    "llm_cap": 25,
    "resolve_cap": 10,
    "min_score": 6,
    "max_employees": 100
  }
};

// Pass every incoming item through and attach the config, so the next nodes can read it with
// $('Config (discovery)').first().json.cfg
return $input.all().map((it, i) => ({ json: Object.assign({}, it.json, { cfg: CONFIG }), pairedItem: { item: i } }));

nodes.name: Config (discovery)
nodes.notes: Profile settings for the discovery lane (sender, models, rules, prompts). Edit here to retarget the pipeline.

nodes.name: Get existing leads
nodes.notes: Reads every lead already in the sheet so nothing is evaluated or contacted twice.

nodes.name: Adzuna search
nodes.notes: Job ads that mention sales hires are a buying signal. The app key comes from a credential (query param app_key); the app id goes in the app_id field.

nodes.name: Prepare weak candidates
nodes.notes: Deduplicates, tracks how long a sales vacancy has been open, pre-scores and caps how many candidates get the paid company lookup.

nodes.name: Dedupe and pre-score
nodes.notes: Merges all sources by domain, stacks signals, applies blocklists, computes the rule-based ICP matrix (0-12) and caps how many go to the LLM.

nodes.name: Ollama: score
nodes.notes: Local LLM scores each candidate against the ICP rubric. The request body is built in the previous node, so model, JSON schema and temperature are explicit.

parameters.content:
## 3. Outreach (weekdays, three slots)
Takes the best pending lead, finds a decision maker (Hunter or Apollo), checks it is not a duplicate, drafts an email and a LinkedIn note with the local LLM, and runs a validation gate. Depending on the send mode the email goes to the lead or to your own inbox as a draft. Anything that fails validation is parked for review.

parameters.jsCode:
// CONFIG for the outreach lane. This is the only place that decides who we target, what we say and how we send.
// To switch to another profile, paste the matching section from config/<profile>.json over this object.
const CONFIG = {
  "timezone": "America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires",
  "language": "en",
  "sender": {
    "name": "Your Name",
    "title": "Business Development",
    "company": "Your Company",
    "signature": "Your Name\nBusiness Development\nYour Company",
    "email": "you@example.com",
    "review_email": "you@example.com"
  },
  "models": {
    "email": "qwen2.5:14b",
    "linkedin": "qwen3:4b",
    "score": "qwen2.5:14b",
    "classify": "llama3.2:3b",
    "followup": "qwen3:4b"
  },
  "contact": {
    "provider": "apollo",
    "min_conf_dm": 60,
    "min_conf_senior": 80,
    "generic_prefixes": [
      "info",
      "support",
      "sales",
      "contact",
      "hello",
      "admin",
      "careers",
      "hr",
      "help",
      "office",
      "team",
      "jobs",
      "recruiting",
      "noreply",
      "no-reply",
      "press",
      "media",
      "billing",
      "accounts",
      "informacion",
      "ventas",
      "contacto",
      "hola",
      "administracion",
      "soporte"
    ],
    "titles": [
      "Founder",
      "Co-Founder",
      "Owner",
      "CEO",
      "Chief Executive Officer",
      "President",
      "Managing Partner",
      "Principal",
      "General Manager"
    ]
  },
  "offer": {
    "email_prompt": "You are {sender_name}, {sender_title} at {sender_company}. {sender_company} is a B2B services consultancy that helps founder-led companies (SaaS, IT services, professional services) build a repeatable sales process: ideal customer profile, playbooks, pricing, CRM and pipeline, with AI only where it removes friction, so growth stops depending on the founder closing every deal. Write a short cold outreach email to {name} ({title}) at {company}. Concrete context you researched about this company, use it as the hook of the first line: {why}. Role they are hiring for (may be empty): {role}. Extra details (may be empty): {details}. If that context is specific (a sales role they posted, a concrete signal), cite it as is without inventing data. If the context is weak, be brief and direct instead of forcing a fake hook. It is FORBIDDEN to use generic filler such as \"recent growth\", \"growing team\", \"scaling fast\" or \"impressed by your work\" without a concrete fact behind it. Naturally, and not as the main hook, mention that a defined sales process means a new sales hire lands on a real pipeline instead of inheriting chaos. Close with a concrete, low-commitment ask (a short 15-minute call this week), never a vague \"let me know how I can help\". Professional, warm, not pushy. Maximum 120 words, no clickbait subject.\nSign as:\n{signature}\nIMPORTANT: the whole email, subject and body, must be written in English. Respond ONLY with a valid JSON object with two fields: subject (short, direct, no emojis) and body (plain text, line breaks as \\n). No other text, no markdown, no code blocks.",
    "linkedin_prompt": "You are {sender_name} at {sender_company}, a B2B services consultancy that helps founder-led companies build a repeatable sales process. Write a short LinkedIn message (under 300 characters) to {name_or_role} at {company}, as a first-touch connection note. Context you researched: {why}. Structure: a brief hook on the concrete signal above if it exists (if it is weak, a short non-generic hook about the type of company, no invented data), one line on what {sender_company} does, and ONE low-commitment closing question (for example whether a quick 15-minute chat makes sense). Never more than one question. Warm, professional, in English, no emojis, no hashtags. Respond ONLY with a valid JSON object with one field: message (the LinkedIn message text). No other text, no markdown, no code blocks."
  },
  "send": {
    "mode": "review",
    "min_score": 6,
    "default_score": 0,
    "daily_cap": 2,
    "min_words": 25,
    "max_words": 170,
    "banned_phrases": [
      "recent growth",
      "growing team",
      "scaling fast",
      "rapid growth",
      "impressed by your work",
      "company culture",
      "expanding team",
      "continued growth"
    ],
    "signature_must_include": "Your Company",
    "optout_line": "P.S. If this is not relevant, just reply \"no\" and I will not follow up."
  }
};

// Pass every incoming item through and attach the config, so the next nodes can read it with
// $('Config (outreach)').first().json.cfg
return $input.all().map((it, i) => ({ json: Object.assign({}, it.json, { cfg: CONFIG }), pairedItem: { item: i } }));

nodes.name: Config (outreach)
nodes.notes: Profile settings for the outreach lane (sender, models, rules, prompts). Edit here to retarget the pipeline.

nodes.name: Pick lead
nodes.notes: Highest score first, oldest row on ties. Stops quietly when the daily cap is reached or nothing qualifies.

nodes.name: Contact provider?
nodes.notes: Config decides which contact-finding service runs: Hunter (domain search) or Apollo (company, people, enrich).

nodes.name: Hunter domain search
nodes.notes: Hunter spends one credit per search. When credits run out the node fails loudly and the Error Workflow sends an alert.

nodes.name: Check duplicates
nodes.notes: Blocks a second email to the same address, or to another person at a company that was already contacted.

nodes.name: Ollama: draft email
nodes.notes: Local LLM writes the cold email as JSON (subject + body). Prompt and tone come from the Config node.

nodes.name: Ollama: draft LinkedIn
nodes.notes: Second, smaller model writes a short LinkedIn connection note.

nodes.name: Validate draft
nodes.notes: Validation gate. Checks length, banned filler phrases, signature, placeholders and language. Only a draft that passes can be sent; the rest is parked for human review.

nodes.name: Route by action
nodes.notes: send = auto mode, email goes to the lead. draft = review mode, email goes to your own inbox. flag = failed validation.

nodes.name: Send email to lead
nodes.notes: The only node that emails a prospect. The row is marked "Sent" only after this node succeeds.

{{ $json.email_body_html }}

Review mode: nothing was sent to the lead. After you send it yourself, set Status to Sent and Sent_on to the date (yyyy-MM-dd) in the sheet so reply and follow-up tracking start.

parameters.content:
## 4. Reply tracking (every 10 minutes)
Watches the inbox, matches replies to leads that were contacted (same sender or a colleague at the same company), ignores out-of-office and bounces, asks the local LLM whether the reply shows real interest, and records it in the sheet.

nodes.name: Config (replies)
nodes.notes: Profile settings for the reply tracking lane (sender, models, rules, prompts). Edit here to retarget the pipeline.

nodes.name: Read leads (replies)
nodes.notes: Runs once per poll (not once per email) to get the pool of contacted leads.

nodes.name: Match replies
nodes.notes: Matches each email to a lead, ignores automatic replies and bounces, and builds the classification request.

nodes.name: Ollama: classify reply
nodes.notes: Local LLM answers one question: does this reply show genuine interest? Output is validated JSON (interested: true/false).

parameters.content:
## 5. Follow-up drafts (weekdays 10:00)
Finds a lead contacted 3+ business days ago with no reply, drafts a very short follow-up and sends it to your own inbox to review and send as a reply in the original thread.

nodes.name: Config (follow-up)
nodes.notes: Profile settings for the follow-up lane (sender, models, rules, prompts). Edit here to retarget the pipeline.

nodes.name: Ollama: draft follow-up
nodes.notes: Local LLM writes a follow-up of at most 50 words.

parameters.subject: =[FOLLOW-UP DRAFT] {{ $json.company }} -> {{ $json.contact_email }}
parameters.message:
=Would reply to: {{ $json.contact_name }} ({{ $json.contact_email }})

Subject: {{ $json.followup_subject }}

{{ $json.followup_body }}

--
Reminder: send it as a reply inside the original thread, not as a new message.

nodes.name: Mark follow-up done
nodes.notes: Marked only after the draft email was sent successfully, so a failure never loses a follow-up.

Emails a summary of which source, signal and vertical converts best: leads, contacted, replies, interested.
